2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that the present respondents as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.65 of 1991 in the 1st Court of Senior Assistant judge, Rajshahi, impleading the present petitioners as defendants for partition of the suit land contending interalia that the suit land measuring .57 acres of land under S.A. Khatian No.178 belonged to Kasimuddin and Samir Mondal in equal share obtained through pattan; Their names were accordingly finally published in S.A. Khatian; The Plaintiff no.1 is the daughter of Kasimuddinis first wife; After the expiry or plaintiff no. l's mother said Kasimuddin again married defendant. Meher Nigar and out of that wedlock plaintiff no.2 was born; While possessing half of the suit land, said Kasimuddin died leaving daughters, widow Meher. Nigar and nephew Abdul Kader as his legal heirs; On the other hand, 3,l mir Mondal while possessing the rest half of the suit land died leaving defendant nos.2 and 3 as his heirs; After the death of Kasimuddin said Meher Nigar received her share from other lands and sold the same to Chandicharan Sarker and ethers; Said Abdul Kader sold his share received from Kasimuddin to Professor Mozaharul, Islam and others; The plaintiffs while enjoying half of the suit land with defendant nos.1-3 in ejmali gave authority to defendant no.1 for recording R.S. Khatian; After getting final record of the R.S. Khatian the plain-tiffs for the first time came to know that it was wrongly recorded in the name of defendants alone and hence constrained to file the suit for partition since there is no earlier partition by metes and bounds. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas learned Advocate appearing for the respondent nos.1-6 in support of the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division submits that the suit for partition simpliciter without prayer for title and khan possession in the suit land is not maintainable. The learned Advocate though admits that the plaintiffs failed to prove their 'pattan' by which they are claiming their title in the suit land but submits that the defendants also failed to prove their case by adducing documents inasmuch as the burden of proof also lies upon the defendants under section 103 of the Evidence Act and there is no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division. 

 13. Admittedly, the plaintiffs' case is that the suit land belonged to their predecessor. Kasimuddin and defendants predecessor Samir Mondal in equal share Obtained through 'pattan'. The very basis of plaintiffs claim is the 'pattan'. But the plaintiffs failed to prove pattani settlement of their predecessor' Kasimuddin. The P. W.1 Abdul Gafur, husband of the plaintiff no.1, deposed that: 

 16. It may he mentioned here that the PW.1 produced 4(four) rent receipts which are marked as exhibit-I series, certified copy of S.A. Khatian No.178, marked as exhibit-2 and certified copy of C.S. Khatian No.244 marked as exhibit 2 f(Kha)'. But the plaintiffs failed to prove pattani settlement in the name of their predecessor Kasimuddin by which they are claiming title in the suit land. 

 19. And thereby made the rule absolute. The High Court Division failed to appreciate that the plaintiffs failed to prove pattani settlement of their predecessor Kasimuddin by which they are claiming their title in the suit land and thereby erred in law to follow the cardinal principle of law that the plaintiffs must prove their own case and they cannot win on the lacuna of the defendants.
